target_customer: Originally patients and clinicians needing at-home blood monitoring (for example clozapine and cancer patients); now independent practices, specialty groups and provider networks buying AI EHR, revenue cycle and ambient documentation tools
problem: Blood monitoring required lab visits and slow results. The company later moved to simplifying healthcare administration with AI tools for documentation, coding and billing.
business_model: Started as a device plus subscription for home blood testing; now B2B software and managed services for health providers (EHR, revenue cycle management, AI scribe, voice agents)
product_category: Digital health devices and healthcare AI software

founders.name: Tanay Tandon
founders.background_notes: Sequoia profile describes a background in machine learning and AI and early prototypes from high school science fairs. No employers or school named there.

founders.name: Deepika Bodapati
founders.background_notes: Sequoia profile says she interned at a molecular imaging research lab at Stanford and built prototypes from school science fairs. Education not stated.

exit.acquirer: Commure (merged, combined company valued at about 6 billion per the announcement)

technical_complexity.rationale: A fingerstick blood analysis device using computer imaging needed hardware, machine learning and clinical validation. Sequoia's profile says a first clinical trial was run in 2016 in Juarez, Mexico, and FDA clearance for home use came only in 2022 per the FDA filings surfaced in search.

defensibility.rationale: Regulatory clearance of a home blood test device is slow to replicate, but the early product was small and the later software business sits in a crowded market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying the original device wedge. In 2023 the company merged with Commure rather than being bought by an incumbent.

market_need_then: Sequoia's profile describes a cancer patient as the first test user who travelled to the founders' Mountain View office for testing, which points to a real pain around frequent blood monitoring. The 2017 TechCrunch launch coverage priced the device at 20 dollars a month and said insurers were hoped for later. No broader market sizing from 2016 was found.

rebrands.to: Commure (merged entity name, Athelas kept as a product brand)
rebrands.why: Merger announcement says the combined company keeps the Commure name; Athelas site now shows Powered by Commure.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found no press on the brand itself, no mascot or community. The company is known for its funding and healthcare product rather than brand.

pivots.from: At-home blood testing device for patients
pivots.to: Healthcare practice software and revenue cycle services, later merged into Commure
pivots.why: Not stated in opened sources; the Commure merger announcement describes a goal of automation infrastructure for health systems.

outcome_analysis: Athelas started as a hardware plus machine learning blood test for home use, ran a clinical trial in 2016 and raised more than 132 million dollars by January 2022 at a reported valuation of at least 1.5 billion. It merged with Commure in October 2023 and the combined company was described as worth about 6 billion, then raised a further 70 million at a reported 7 billion in May 2026. Layoffs were reported shortly after the merger. Its path shows a successful move from a regulated device into healthcare software, but the sources do not detail revenue.
notes: Round stage labels were not stated in the company posts, so stage is other. Aggregators call the January 2022 raise a Series B or C and also list a 2021 Series B of 72 million, which was not confirmed by a second named outlet and is not recorded as a round. The 132 million figure covers two consecutive rounds led by General Catalyst and Tribe Capital with no split given. The 2023 merger included a 70 million General Catalyst investment per search snippets (Endpoints, Fierce Healthcare) that were not opened, so it is not recorded as a round. The 2022 raise and the 2023 valuation of 6 billion are stated by the company. No dated competitor source for 2016 was found; Sequoia only mentions unnamed YC peers. Athelas status is Active in the directory while the exit is recorded as a merger.
